target_customer: Designers and product and marketing teams who make animated content for videos, websites and apps
problem: Motion design tools such as After Effects are complex and keyframe based, so many designers cannot animate quickly or collaborate on motion.
business_model: Freemium B2B and prosumer SaaS subscription for a web motion design tool

founders.name: Sébastien Robaszkiewicz
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; called co-founder in a 2025 article. Background not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Etienne Albert
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; called co-founder in a 2025 article. Background not found in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser based animation engine with real time rendering and video, GIF and Lottie export is demanding for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Template libraries and workflow habits help, but animation features can be matched by Figma, Adobe or startups.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or acquisition found in the sources.

market_need_then: Designers were moving to Figma and wanted a similarly simple tool for motion, while animated content demand rose.

branding.domain_note: Uses jitter.video; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Fast, simple and collaborative per a June 2025 article

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt Design Tool of the Year 2024 listed on its site; Figma plugin reported at 170k to 300k installs by differing sources.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong designer community presence and awards claimed on its site, but the name is a common word and the founders' brand story was not found.

outcome_analysis: Jitter is an active Paris based motion design tool that grew through a Figma plugin and templates, with claims of tens of thousands of monthly users and 20,000 creative teams. Public funding data is only small YC era amounts, so the scale of capital behind it is unknown. Growth looks product led and capital efficient, but this is not verified.
notes: Funding seen only on aggregators (CB Insights 500K total including a convertible note and Norte Ventures, others 150K from YC), not cross-checked, so no rounds recorded. Batch conflict: shard and one search say Winter 2020, another snippet says W21. Competitors left empty: After Effects appears only in a 2025 article, and no source near 2020 was found. Completeness pass: the 150K pre-seed in 2020-02 rests on a single database (Seedtable); CB Insights instead shows a 500K convertible note on 2020-01-01, conflicting and not recorded. No later funding found.
